votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

posts.text: Congratulations @Jim_Jordan, @GOPMajorityWhip and @RepLisaMcClain!

215 constituents helped with issues like back VA benefits, owed Social Security, and missing IRS refunds in October. Since January, my office has returned over $3.2 million back to TX-31 constituents! https://t.co/nv6qUFColR
Nidal Hasan caused immeasurable wounds to our community. The victims, survivors, their families and our community deserve to see justice finally served.

Our hearts are with the family, friends, and fellow Soldiers of the Soldier who tragically lost their life during a training incident at Fort Hood. We lift them up in prayer and ask for comfort, strength, and peace during this incredibly difficult time. We also pray for the healing and recovery of the injured Soldier and for all those affected by this tragedy.

Twenty-five years later, we remember the lives forever changed by the attacks on our nation. We honor and mourn those we lost, remember the families affected, and pay tribute to the courage and sacrifice of the first responders who answered the call.
We will never forget. https://t.co/6G2vGa1oAP

Please join me in welcoming Devin, one of the new fall interns on Team Carter. Devin is a sophomore majoring in Business Management at Texas State University- Round Rock. He’s also the founder and president of Round Rock Business Club. Welcome, Devin!
Interns are a valued part of my team and get paid experience in government, public policy and constituent services during their time here. If you’re interested in interning, visit: https://t.co/zvna9600J2

Congratulations to Williamson County Precinct 2 Constable Jeff Anderson and his Command Staff for completing the FBI-Law Enforcement Executive Development Association program. The FBI-LEEDA program expands law enforcement leadership through training, education and networking and their completion speaks to the deep commitment these officers have to WilCo’s public safety. 

We are blessed to have such dedicated officers protecting our communities in TX-31!

I'm aware of reports that a military helicopter has gone down in Salado Texas's 31st district. While we wait for additional information, our prayers are with any occupants on board. My team and I will continue to monitor.

Texas has lost a trailblazer. I’m deeply saddened to hear of the passing of one of my dearest friends, Kay Granger. For decades, she led with grace and a deep love of Texas. Kay was someone whose counsel I valued and character I admired. While we all mourn her passing, I hope everyone also celebrates her remarkable service. Texas is a better place because of Kay’s leadership.

City of Belton employee Ethan Van de Plas was working near Nolan Creek when a woman jumped into the high water. The situation quickly became dangerous, but Ethan sprang into action. He jumped into the rain-swollen creek and pulled her to safety. I recently honored Ethan for his selfless service with a congressional certificate of recognition and an American flag flown over the US Capitol in his honor.
Ethan plans to join the military soon, and I have no doubt he has the bravery and selflessness to succeed. Well done, Ethan!

He jumped into the rain-swollen creek and pulled her to safety. I recently honored Ethan for his selfless service with a congressional certificate of recognition and an American flag flown over the US Capitol in his honor.
Ethan plans to join the military soon, and I have no doubt he has the bravery and selflessness to succeed. Well done, Ethan!
@RepDebDingell Erika and I are so sorry for your family's loss.
Erika and I saddened to hear of the passing of American patriot Lindsey Graham. Our condolences go out to his family, friends and staff.

When Joel, a veteran injured in Operation Inherent Resolve, reached out for assistance with his military personnel records and combat awards, we went to work. Within 2 weeks, his records were received and within 3, his awards were ready to be presented to him for outstanding service.

It was a pleasure recognizing Joel for his brave service to the nation. It is because of warriors like Joel that America will celebrate 250 years of freedom and liberty next week.

The passing of Josh Baer is a huge loss for Texas. He was a disruptor, a brilliant innovator, and had immense enthusiasm for helping others succeed. My sincerest condolences to Josh’s family, friends, and the @CapitalFactory team. He will be greatly missed by me and my staff. https://t.co/AjlKMAfL4E

Every year, I nominate incredible young people to America’s military academies. It’s a grueling process that requires strong academics, extracurricular participation, grit, and determination. I was pleased to send off our TX-31 class of 2030 appointees at my annual Academy Salute over the weekend. Join me in wishing them well as they depart on the adventure of a lifetime!

Interns are a valued part of my office. Please join me in welcoming this year’s summer intern class to Team Carter! We are glad you’ll be joining us for the next couple of months.
My office offers paid internships to college students who have completed their freshman year. These internships provide valuable experience in the legislative process, constituent services, and communications. To learn more, visit: https://t.co/zvna9600J2
PASSED 400-15! That's delivering for America’s service members and veterans. https://t.co/zAQCI3XA76
Praying for everyone at the White House Correspondents Dinner!

TX-31 EMERGENCY ALERT: An evacuation order has been issued for areas near Shady River and Good Water RV parks in Georgetown due to flash flooding. Evacuate immediately to higher ground. Do not drive into flooded roadways. Temporary evacuation site at Georgetown Church of the Nazarene- 4051 E University Ave. Georgetown, TX 78626

As the chairman of the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee on Appropriations, I'm proud that the bill released today ensures our heroes have access to quality health care, mental health services, and improved housing. I look forward to moving this bill through the appropriations process with Chairman Cole.

I was honored to receive an award from the National Guard Association of Texas recognizing my commitment to our National Guardsmen and my support for their mission.

I’m grateful for the opportunity to stand with the men and women of the Texas National Guard and will continue working to ensure they have the resources and support they deserve as they serve our state and nation.

Great to spend some time today with our friends from the VFW who came to Washington to visit with our office. These men and women served our country with honor, and it’s always a privilege to hear directly from our veterans about the issues that matter most to them and their families.

For far too long, the Iranian regime has pursued nuclear capabilities while exporting violence and supporting terrorist networks that threaten the United States, our allies, and stability around the world. Their actions have endangered American lives and undermined peace in an already volatile region.

The President has made clear that the United States will always seek peace, but we will never hesitate to defend our people and our national interests. Iran’s continued hostility and disregard for international norms have brought us to a serious and consequential moment.

America must stand firm in protecting our citizens, supporting our allies, and upholding peace through strength.

Please keep the men and women of our Armed Forces in your prayers as they carry out this mission, along with the families who support them from home. Their service represents the very best of our nation. May God protect them, and may God continue to bless the United States of America.

Last night, I took my seat in the House Chamber to hear President Trump outline the progress made during his first year back in office and share his priorities for the year ahead.

Under President Trump’s leadership, we are restoring economic strength, reasserting American leadership on the world stage, securing our border, and putting American families first. His commitment to the America First agenda is not just rhetoric. It is delivering real results and renewed confidence across our nation.

I was proud to stand in support of an agenda that prioritizes our workers, our military, our law enforcement, and our values. There is more work to be done, but the direction is clear and the momentum is strong. I remain committed to partnering with President Trump to advance policies that keep our nation strong, secure, and prosperous for generations to come.

I left the chamber grateful for the trust Central Texans have placed in me and more committed than ever to serving faithfully and responsibly, always with future generations in mind.

A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
